summary: Tanso Hirose (1782–1856) was a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and Japanology. He studied at Kamei Juku (~1797–1801) and under Hōdō, and founded Kangien in 1801.

Tanuja Ajotikar specializes in Indology and computational linguistics. She held posts at Harvard University, as Co-director of Sanskrit Department India Programs at Maharishi Vedic University, and as Assistant Professor at the Sanskrit Library (attested 2024–2025).

Tanzan Hara (1819–1892) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He served at the Ministry of Religion (1872–1874), the University of Tokyo (1879), and Komazawa University (1891).
Tao Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (2017–2026). In 2026, Chen served as a Postdoctoral Fellow at Fo Guang Shan.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. Jiang held a position as Associate Professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University (attested 2011).
Tao Jin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Jin completed a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Pan earned a BA from Fudan University (completed by 2010) and a Magister Artium from the University of Munich.

Tara Doyle is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. At Emory University, she served as a lecturer in religious studies and director of the Tibetan Studies Program (attested 2003), and later as Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Tarapada Chowdhury (1907–1964) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Edward Hamilton Johnston by 1950 and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Patna College (attested 1950).
Tara Sheemar is a historian and Indologist who completed a PhD at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2011. She was appointed Associate Professor at Janki Devi Memorial College in 2003.
Tarab Tulku (1934–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. From circa 1962 to 1998, he held a post at the University of Copenhagen and worked as a curator at the Royal Danish Library.

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati (1812–1885) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University (~1845–1874) and as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College.

Tariq Rafeeq Khan specializes in philosophy and Indology, earning a PhD from Jiwaji University (2017–2020). In 2022, he was appointed Assistant Professor at the Islamic University of Science and Technology.

Taro Tokutake is an Indologist and historian educated at Hiroshima University (BA, 2015–2019) and Kyoto University (PhD, 2021–2024). He held visiting postdoctoral fellowships at CNRS (2024–2025), Paris Cité University (2025–2026), and the University of Edinburgh (2026).

Tarthang Tulku (born 1935) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar trained at Tarthang Monastery. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center (~1969), and founded the Nyingma Institute in 1972.

Tashi Densapa (born 1918) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978 and 2002) and as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a Tibetologist who studied at University College, Toronto, Magdalen College, Cambridge, and Harvard. She held posts at Georgetown University and the University of Virginia, where she was co-director of the Tibet Center (attested 2026).

Tashi Samphel is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an Associate Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering (born 1960) works in Tibetology, history, and linguistics. He served at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1979–1992), became Director of the Amnye Machen Institute (~1992), and was a Professor at CIHTS (attested 2014–2019).
Tat'yana Katenina (1926–1987) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at Saint Petersburg State University from circa 1944 to 1949 and served there as a Docent beginning in 1948.
